verifications.claim: Saudi Arabia has officially declared that Eid al-Fitr 2026 will fall on Friday, March 20, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Saudi Arabia announced today (March 18, 2026) that the first day of Eid al Fitr will fall on March 20'; R2: 'Saudi Arabia just confirmed the date of Eid al-Fitr 2026 as Friday, March 20'; R3: 'Eid Al Fitr 2026 will begin on Friday, March 20'; R5: 'Saudi Arabia has officially announced that Eid al-Fitr will be observed on March 20, 2026'; R6: 'Eid ul Fitr 2026 was announced as being on Friday, March 20, in Saudi Arabia'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly state Saudi Arabia's official declaration of Eid al-Fitr on March 20, 2026.

verifications.claim: The Shawwal crescent moon was not sighted on the evening of Wednesday, March 18, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'after the Shawwal crescent moon was not sighted'; R3: 'attempts to sight the Shawwal crescent moon were unsuccessful... moon was not seen anywhere'; R6: 'unsuccessfully attempted to sight the new crescent moon on Wednesday'
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly confirm no sighting on Wednesday, March 18, 2026; minor ambiguity from other sources' phrasing but no direct contradiction for this date.

verifications.reasoning: Sources support via 30-day Ramadan and Eid on March 20 implying Thursday March 19 as last fast day, but no direct statement of the exact phrase.

verifications.claim: The Holy Mosques in Saudi Arabia confirmed the end of Ramadan following the completion of the 30-day fast, according to Manchester Evening News.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: R1 references X/@HaramainInfo (Holy Mosques account) but not MEN; R3 (MEN): 'Saudi authorities... Supreme Court' no Holy Mosques; R6 (MEN): 'officials in the kingdom' no Holy Mosques or 30-day confirmation attributed to them
verifications.reasoning: Holy Mosques referenced indirectly in R1, but Manchester Evening News sources (R3, R6) attribute to other authorities, not Holy Mosques; claim misattributes source.
